task:
Make the freelance finance tracker ready for its owner to use day to day on their phone. Keep every existing feature, test and screen working.

1. Bug: renaming a category (renameCategory in src/lib/categories.ts, for both default and custom categories) must also update every saved receipt whose category is the old name (compared case-insensitively) to the new name, so that afterwards no receipt uses the old name, getAllCategories no longer lists the old name, syncCategoriesWithReceipts does not bring it back, and isCategoryInUse(newName) is true when receipts used the old name. Receipts in other categories, and every other field of the updated receipts, stay exactly as they were. A rename that fails (invalid name, name already exists, category not found) changes no receipts.
2. Bug: mileage accepts decimal miles. validateMileageMiles accepts any number greater than 0 with up to 1 decimal place (12.5 is valid; 0, negative numbers, 12.55 and text are not), the Miles field on the Add mileage screen accepts "12.5", and the deduction shown and saved uses the decimal value.
3. Dashboard: the Receipt and Mileage add buttons and the "Receipt saved" confirmation never cover the Recent activity list; every activity row shows its amount, and the list can scroll past the buttons. The bottom tab labels (Dashboard, Receipts, Mileage, Settings) are fully visible on a 390x844 phone screen.
4. Add receipt: the screen title appears once (in the header only); the date picker icon sits inside the Date field; no empty gaps larger than the standard spacing between fields; the "Scan receipt" button is not shown while scanning isn't available.
5. Settings: App lock appears once (the switch row; no separate App lock button). The other entries (Tax settings, Categories, Export, Backup & restore, Delete all data, View Terms and Privacy Policy) are list rows with a chevron, not outlined buttons; Delete all data is shown in the error color, last, separated from the others.

wrong_tests.fix: Replace the U+2011 hyphen with a regular ASCII hyphen or delete the comment, and rename the folder to "__tests__" (no leading space) so Jest can discover the test.

wrong_tests.reason: The test file resides in the incorrectly named " __tests__" folder, preventing it from being executed.
wrong_tests.fix: Move the file to a correctly named "__tests__/acceptance" directory without a leading space.

review.feedback: Fix the test suite naming issues and the syntax error, ensure renameCategory updates receipts atomically and rolls back correctly on any failure, and adjust validation messages to match the required specifications. After these changes, run the full test suite to confirm all requirements are satisfied.
unproven: The acceptance test file __tests__/acceptance/m7-category-rename.test.ts contains a non‑ASCII hyphen (U+2011) in a comment, causing a SyntaxError when the test suite is run. This prevents the tests from executing and masks potential failures in the implementation.

Similarly, other acceptance test files are placed in a directory named " __tests__" (note the leading space) which is not the standard "__tests__" path. As a result, Jest does not discover or run these tests, so many requirements are not being validated.

It attempts to revert changes by reloading data after a failure, but the rollback only restores the category mapping and does not revert any receipt updates that may have been partially applied before the error was thrown.

This discrepancy will cause tests checking the exact error strings to fail.

security.summary: Security review of the freelance‑finance‑tracker identifies multiple high‑severity code findings (unfixed vulnerable dependencies and a data‑reset photo leak) and several medium‑severity logic gaps (backup restore path traversal, size‑based DOS, brute‑force lockout, and CSV injection). All findings are currently open and must be addressed before the app can be released to production.

findings.issue: restoreBackup writes files using the photoUri values stored in the backup payload, allowing an attacker‑controlled path to be written outside the app’s sandbox (path‑traversal).
findings.fix: Ignore any photoUri in the backup data; when restoring images, always write to a trusted internal directory (FileSystem.documentDirectory) and verify the resolved path stays within that directory.

findings.issue: No size checks on the encrypted backup blob or on the number of receipts/mileage entries, enabling a maliciously large backup to exhaust memory or CPU during restore.
findings.fix: Reject encrypted backup blobs larger than 10 MiB before decryption and enforce sensible caps (e.g., ≤10 000 receipts and ≤5 000 mileage entries) in validateBackupStructure.

findings.issue: restoreBackup allows unlimited incorrect passphrase attempts, permitting offline brute‑force attacks on the backup encryption key.
findings.fix: Implement exponential back‑off after each failed attempt (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, …) and lock the restore UI after five consecutive failures; store the failure count in memory and reset on app restart.

findings.issue: CSV export concatenates user‑provided fields without proper escaping, allowing CSV injection (e.g., formulas like =cmd|…) when the file is opened in spreadsheet software.
findings.fix: Replace the manual string building with a robust CSV library such as csv‑stringify, ensuring commas, quotes, newlines and leading characters are escaped according to RFC 4180.

ledger.issue: clearAllData removes encrypted records but does not delete photo files referenced by receipt.photoUri, leaving images on the device after a data reset and exposing user‑private data.
ledger.fix: Update clearAllData to iterate over all receipts, collect any photoUri values, and delete the corresponding files with expo‑file‑system before clearing the encrypted store.

history.reason: re-checked by Claude: clearAllData (alias for deleteAllData) now calls deleteAllPhotos() before and after store.wipe(), and deleteAllPhotos deletes the entire receipt-photos directory via expo-file-system, removing all photo files regardless of individual photoUri tracking.

ledger.issue: restoreBackup writes files using the photoUri values stored in the backup payload, allowing an attacker‑controlled path to be written outside the app’s sandbox (path‑traversal).
ledger.fix: Ignore any photoUri in the backup data; when restoring images, always write to a trusted internal directory (FileSystem.documentDirectory) and verify the resolved path stays within that directory.

ledger.issue: No size checks on the encrypted backup blob or on the number of receipts/mileage entries, enabling a maliciously large backup to exhaust memory or CPU during restore.
ledger.fix: Reject encrypted backup blobs larger than 10 MiB before decryption and enforce sensible caps (e.g., ≤10 000 receipts and ≤5 000 mileage entries) in validateBackupStructure.

ledger.issue: restoreBackup allows unlimited incorrect passphrase attempts, permitting offline brute‑force attacks on the backup encryption key.
ledger.fix: Implement exponential back‑off after each failed attempt (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, …) and lock the restore UI after five consecutive failures; store the failure count in memory and reset on app restart.

ledger.issue: CSV export concatenates user‑provided fields without proper escaping, allowing CSV injection (e.g., formulas like =cmd|…) when the file is opened in spreadsheet software.
ledger.fix: Replace the manual string building with a robust CSV library such as csv‑stringify, ensuring commas, quotes, newlines and leading characters are escaped according to RFC 4180.

ledger.issue: node‑forge 1.4.0 contains CVE‑2026‑85393 (signature forgery in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification); no fixed release exists.
ledger.fix: No fixed release exists yet: monitor the advisory and upgrade as soon as one ships; confirm whether the package is only a build-time dependency. Replace node‑forge with a maintained crypto library (e.g., noble‑ciphers) for any RSA/PKCS#1 operations, or wait for a patched version and update the dependency accordingly.

ledger.issue: braces 3.0.3 is vulnerable to CVE‑2026‑93687 (Denial‑of‑Service via deeply nested glob patterns); no fix is currently available.
ledger.fix: Upgrade to a non‑vulnerable version if released, or replace its usage (e.g., glob pattern handling) with a safer alternative that does not rely on braces.
